title: Nasdaq Hits New Record as Stock Futures Remain Steady: Live Updates】
body:
U.S. equity futures were essentially flat on Wednesday morning, as investors digested the Nasdaq Composite’s surge to a fresh all‑time high on Tuesday and weighed the impact of easing oil prices and lower Treasury yields amid tentative signs of a diplomatic thaw between Washington and Tehran. The modest movement in futures—S&P 500 futures up 0.09% and Nasdaq futures unchanged—suggests that market participants are adopting a wait‑and‑see stance, balancing optimism over the tech rally with lingering uncertainty over geopolitical and macroeconomic risks.

The Nasdaq’s climb was driven by a broad‑based rally in high‑growth technology stocks, which together pushed the index past its previous intraday peak and closed at a record level. Heavyweights such as Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Alphabet all posted double‑digit gains, buoyed by strong earnings reports and continued demand for artificial‑intelligence chips and cloud services. The index’s momentum was further reinforced by a surge in semiconductor manufacturers, whose shares rallied on news of expanded capacity and new product launches aimed at meeting the soaring appetite for AI‑driven workloads.

While the tech sector captured headlines, the broader market backdrop was shaped by a modest retreat in oil prices and a dip in long‑term Treasury yields. Crude settled lower after reports that diplomatic channels between the United States and Iran were being explored, dampening fears of an escalation that could have disrupted global oil supplies. At the same time, the 10‑year Treasury yield slipped below 4.6%, reflecting investor relief over the prospect of a more stable geopolitical environment and the continued expectation of a gradual easing of monetary policy by the Federal Reserve later this year.

Analysts caution, however, that the Nasdaq’s record run may be vulnerable to a confluence of headwinds. Inflation data due later this month could force the Fed to reconsider its rate‑cut timeline, while the lingering threat of a broader conflict in the Middle East remains a wildcard. Moreover, the technology sector’s rapid valuation expansion has sparked concerns about a potential correction, especially if earnings growth begins to lag behind the lofty expectations baked into current stock prices. “The market is riding a wave of optimism, but the underlying fundamentals—particularly in the AI space—still need to prove they can sustain this level of growth,” said a senior equity strategist at a major brokerage firm.

In contrast, the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average showed more modest gains on Tuesday, underscoring the Nasdaq’s outsized influence on today’s futures market. Defensive sectors such as utilities and consumer staples remained relatively flat, indicating that investors are still seeking safe‑haven assets amid the lingering geopolitical uncertainty. The modest rise in S&P 500 futures suggests that broader market sentiment remains cautiously bullish, buoyed by the strength of the tech rally but tempered by the need for clearer signals from both the Fed and the diplomatic front.

Looking ahead, market direction will likely hinge on several key events. The upcoming release of the Consumer Price Index and core inflation figures will be closely watched for clues about the Fed’s policy path. Simultaneously, any concrete progress in U.S.–Iran talks could further calm oil markets and reinforce the risk‑off sentiment that has kept bond yields in check. If the geopolitical situation stabilizes and inflation data shows a continued easing trend, the Nasdaq could extend its record‑setting run, pulling the broader market higher. Conversely, any escalation in the Middle East or a surprise uptick in inflation could quickly reverse the optimism, prompting a pullback across equities and a resurgence of safe‑haven buying. Investors, therefore, remain poised at a crossroads, ready to react to the next wave of data and diplomatic developments.
